# Downwinders Advocates

> Independent, privately owned company that helps families prepare and file federal Radiation
> Exposure Compensation Act (RECA) claims. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the U.S. Department
> of Justice or any government agency. Not a law firm.

## What RECA is
The Radiation Exposure Compensation Act is a federal program administered by the U.S. Department of
Justice. It compensates people who developed certain illnesses after exposure to radiation from
above-ground nuclear weapons testing or from uranium mining, milling and ore transport.

## Covered areas as of the 2025 reauthorization
- Statewide: Utah, New Mexico, Idaho
- Arizona, these counties only: Coconino, Yavapai, Navajo, Apache, Gila, Mohave
- Nevada, these counties only: Eureka, Lander, Lincoln, Nye, White Pine, and part of Clark
- Manhattan Project waste areas in parts of Missouri, Tennessee, Kentucky and Alaska
- NOT covered: Montana, Colorado, Guam

## Key facts
- Filing deadline: December 31, 2027. Statutory. Cannot be waived.
- Compensation: up to $100,000. Manhattan Project waste claimants receive $50,000 or $25,000.
- Surviving spouses, children, parents and in some cases grandchildren may file for a deceased person.
- Melanoma does not qualify under any category.
- Kidney and bladder cancer are separate categories and are not interchangeable.
- Uranium workers are covered for nonmalignant respiratory and renal conditions, not only cancer.
- Free assistance is available from federally funded RESEP clinics.
- Only the U.S. Department of Justice determines eligibility. No company or attorney can promise approval.
